what: Cost of --debug-numeric relative to a plain --debug trace, re-measured because the figures carried in REVIEW_GPU (11.6x, trace 254 MB) have no surviving artifact or recorded conditions.
findings: Trace size ratio is stable at 1.98x across all three scales: --debug-numeric roughly doubles the trace, it does not multiply it by ten.
Wall-clock ratio over --debug is not a single number. It rises with scale (2.1x, 5.3x, 7.2x) because a fixed ~7-11 s of model load and untraced collection is amortised.

With that fixed cost subtracted, the tracing-only ratio is 10x / 22.5x / 14.9x. These are small absolute differences (1 s vs 10 s, 2 s vs 45 s, 9 s vs 134 s) and are noisy, but they bracket the 11.6x that REVIEW_GPU carried, so that figure is plausible as a tracing-only ratio.

Trace volume is 3.63 MB per collected document with numeric on at this model size. The 254 MB in the old record corresponds to roughly 70 collected documents for a 0.6B model, or fewer for a larger one. The original condition was never recorded, so it cannot be pinned down.
Cost is governed by --collect-limit, not --limit: the trace is written during the collection pass only. Evaluating 64 documents and collecting 8 costs the same trace as evaluating 8 and collecting 8.
not_verified: The original 11.6x / 254 MB conditions (model, task, document count) remain unknown; this is a fresh measurement under stated conditions, not a reproduction of that one.
axes/extremes cost (Qwen3-8B, arc_easy, 8 documents: 11x evaluation, ~196 s aggregation, ~280 MB per document) was not re-measured: Qwen3-8B needs ~16.4 GB of download against 19 GB of free disk.
